div.head: Iudex 4
div.ab: Nys nanwiht unrihtlycre ðonne ys þæt man medsceattas onfó for domum: for ðan þe ða medsceattas ablendað þæra wisra manna heortan ⁊ hi forcyrrað ðæra rihtwisra manna word.
Et nichil iniustius est quam susceptio munerum pro iudicio subuertendo, quia munera excecant cor sapientum et subuertunt uerba iustorum.

Nichts ist unmoralischer, als [dás] ist, dass für Richtersprüche Lohngelder angenommen werden, weil die Lohngelder die Herzen der weisen Männer verblenden und sie verkehren der gerechten Männer Worte.
Nothing is more immoral than [this]: that bribes are accepted for judgments, because bribes blind the hearts of wise men and pervert the words of the righteous.
Nothing is more unjust than one who accepts bribes for his judgements, because the bribes blind a wise man’s heart, and they subvert the words of the more righteous man.
